t0112_correction: T0112 REMAINS IMMUTABLE AND ITS CERTIFICATE EVIDENCE IS UNCHANGED AND CORRECT. Its separate_finding_not_touched field is not. It stated that stayconnect-tc-setup.service was 'ALSO failing 203/EXEC: it names /opt/stayconnect/deploy/scripts/tc-setup.sh, which does not exist on the appliance.' BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG. The file existed (-rwxr-xr-x, 1358 bytes, dated 2026-07-17). The failure was ExecMainStatus=1, not 203/EXEC: the journal shows the script RAN on 2026-09-01T03:41:49Z, primed ens160 successfully, and then exited 1 on 'Cannot find device "br-lan"' - a bridge that does not exist under the dynamic guest-network architecture. The error came from reading the installer self-test's SANDBOX prediction (its fixture had no such file) as appliance fact, and from reading `systemctl show ExecStart`, which prints the unit's DEFINITION with status=0/0, as a run result. Neither the certificate diagnosis nor any other T0112 finding is affected.
tc_classification: B - SUPERSEDED_LEGACY_UNIT, established by read-only diagnosis and confirmed here. netd owns the entire kernel realization: shape.Client.EnsureBridgeInfra creates the guest-bridge egress HTB root, the IFB device, the IFB root, the ingress qdisc and the mirred redirect, idempotently, on every acctd submit pass - so a boot with zero tc state is rebuilt by the first pass and no priming unit is required. netd NEVER deletes a root qdisc. The retired unit contradicted current architecture in four independent ways: it primed ens160 (WAN/management) and br-lan (nonexistent); its script documented per-session classids as '1:<last octet>' when the scheme is MinorForIP in 0x1000-0x1fff plus SHARED groups in 0x2000-0x2fff; it named scd as the runtime owner of shaping, which scd has not been for a long time; and its prime() opened with `tc qdisc del dev <IF> root`, which against a live guest bridge would delete netd's root and every class beneath it. Nothing depended on it: acctd referenced it only through non-blocking After=/Wants=.
retirement: REPOSITORY: deploy/systemd/stayconnect-tc-setup.service and deploy/scripts/tc-setup.sh deleted; the After=/Wants= edges removed from stayconnect-acctd.service; the Makefile phase2-install target no longer chmods, installs or `enable --now`s it; the stale ownership comment in internal/shape/shape.go corrected; SYSTEM_OVERVIEW and DEPLOYMENT_APPLIANCE corrected as CURRENT guidance and PHASE19_ASSESSMENT and PHASE19_FINAL_REPORT labelled unmistakably HISTORICAL. APPLIANCE: the unit file and the script were preserved as non-executable evidence under /root/retired-tc-setup/, then removed; the corrected acctd unit was installed and daemon-reload run WITHOUT restarting acctd; the failed state was cleared. The unit's own ExecStart and ExecStop were never run - the legacy teardown deletes root qdiscs and must never execute again.
legacy_qdisc_removed: The inert HTB root the retired unit had primed on ens160 on 2026-09-01 was removed, under explicit authorization and after proving ownership: it carried direct_packets_stat 0 with the tc-setup-specific 1:fffe aggregate and a 10: fq_codel leaf, none of which netd creates, while netd reported 0 managed classes, 0 nft elements and 0 live Sessions. ens160 has returned to the kernel default fq_codel. THE NETD-OWNED INFRASTRUCTURE IS BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED: br-g-00d1fa1a still carries htb 1: root plus ingress ffff: at direct_packets_stat 11718 (identical before and after) and ifb-g-00d1fa1a still carries its htb 1: root, its counter advancing only with live traffic. ens192 was not touched. No nft command was issued at any point; the ruleset's structural digest (counters normalised) is stable at 977b6d691e1439e5f0b84b9ab2c09f1e32104bfcc3420343a81adce966f607de and is now recorded on the appliance as a baseline for future comparison.
installer_defect_closed: The external-helper broadening delivered at T0112 installed any repository script whose BASENAME matched an absolute Exec path. That would have re-armed this very unit: stayconnect-tc-setup named /opt/stayconnect/deploy/scripts/tc-setup.sh, the repository still shipped a tc-setup.sh, and the installer would have written it out - turning a dormant, harmless failure into a script whose first act is a root-qdisc deletion. It would not have STARTED it; it did not need to, because acctd's Wants= edge pulled it in on every acctd restart, which is exactly what happened on 2026-09-01. Helper installation is now driven by an ENUMERATED contract (EXTERNAL_HELPER_CONTRACT) naming unit, destination and source, one line per helper; a filename match is no longer authority. A retired unit whose helper is absent is reported and skipped rather than aborting an unrelated install, while a genuinely current enabled unit with a missing or non-executable program still fails closed. Two adversarial cases prove both halves, including that the T0112 certificate-manager installation still works.
new_standing_audit: deploy/scripts/check-appliance-units.sh closes the class of defect rather than the instance: it refuses any StayConnect unit in a failed state and any unit that COULD run whose declared programs are missing or non-executable. Dormancy is proven rather than assumed - a unit is excused only when it is disabled AND inactive AND pulled in by nothing - so the Central-only stayconnect-ctrlapi and stayconnect-web-admin units an edge appliance legitimately carries are reported as deliberately dormant instead of failing a check nobody would then keep switched on. Six self-test cases, all green on Linux, including the disabled-but-still-pulled-in trap that kept tc-setup running. Installed on .25, where it now reports PASS with 10 units checked and 2 deliberately dormant.
